The new heaven, new earth and new Jerusalem (verses 1–8)

The new heaven and the new earth will not be separated from one another.

The glorified bodies of the saints will belong to a heavenly condition.

The former world, with all its unrest and conflict, will have passed away.

The declaration that there will be no sea fittingly represents freedom from conflicting passions, temptation, distress, uncertainty and fear—everything that divides believers or interrupts their fellowship.

The new Jerusalem is God's church in its renewed and perfected condition, the church triumphant.

Her blessedness comes entirely from God and rests completely upon him.

God's presence with his people will no longer be interrupted as it is here.

He will dwell among them continually.

Every effect of former suffering will disappear.

His children have often wept because of their sin, their troubles and the distress of the church.

But in that state there will be neither the signs nor the memory of former sorrows.

Christ makes everything new.

When we genuinely desire the Redeemer to renew our hearts and nature, we can trust him to bring our circumstances also into the fullness of happiness he promises.

The certainty of this future rests on the character of God himself.

He calls himself Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the End, pledging that he will fulfill what he has said.

Worldly and sinful pleasures resemble poisoned, muddy water.

Even the best earthly comforts are like a small quantity of water stored in a cistern.

When we make idols of them, they become broken cisterns and yield only disappointment.

But Christ's gifts are like water flowing from an abundant spring: pure, refreshing, inexhaustible and everlasting.

The sanctifying comforts of the Holy Spirit prepare God's people for heavenly joy, like streams providing water in the wilderness.

Those described as cowardly shrink from the hardships of true religion because they do not believe.

They may refuse the cross of Christ while still rushing into severe wickedness.

The terrors of the first death are followed by something incomparably worse for the unrepentant: everlasting death.

The heavenly city's glory and security (verses 9–21)

God gives his holy angels many different tasks.

Sometimes they sound trumpets announcing divine judgments and warnings to an unthinking world.

At other times they reveal heavenly realities to those who will inherit salvation.

Those seeking a clear view of heaven should ascend, as it were, the mountain of meditation and faith.

The vision portrays the perfected, triumphant church in all her glory.

Her glory rests on her relationship with Christ.

Heaven's happiness consists in fellowship with God and becoming like him.

The image changes from bride to city, reminding us to draw the broad spiritual meaning rather than try to interpret every architectural detail literally.

The city's wall signifies complete security.

No evil or enemy can harm anyone who dwells there.

Its enormous size assures us that there is room for all God's people.

The foundation of its safety is God's promise and power, and what Christ has purchased.

The twelve kinds of precious stone may represent the varied beauties of gospel doctrine, the Spirit's graces, or the perfections of Christ himself.

Henry offers these as possible meanings, not as an identification of each individual stone.

The city has gates because everyone whom God has made holy is freely admitted.

Its gates are pearls, pointing toward Christ, the Pearl of great price, who is our way to the Father.

Its street is pure gold, clear as glass.

What people prize most highly on earth is beneath the feet of the saints in heaven.

The redeemed enjoy rest, but not sleep, inactivity or idleness.

They have joyful fellowship both with God and with one another.

Even these magnificent images are only faint representations of the happiness to come.

The Lord God and the Lamb illuminate the city (verses 22–27)

Direct and perfect fellowship with God will more than replace the religious ordinances believers now need on earth.

The absence of a separate temple reveals the unity and equal deity of the Son with the Father.

Without the sun's light, this world would be dreadful.

But in heaven God's glory gives light, and the Lamb is its lamp.

Through Christ, God becomes an everlasting source of understanding and joy to the redeemed.

There is no night and no need to close the city's gates.

All is peaceful, secure and full of divine light.

No sinful, unclean, idolatrous, false or deceitful thing can enter.

Everyone there has been made perfectly holy.

For now, even the saints struggle with remaining corruption, which interrupts worship and communion with God.

But on entering heaven's true sanctuary, they are washed through Christ's blood and presented to the Father without stain.

No hypocrite or person devoted to falsehood can enter.

Because nothing impure enters God's heavenly city, these glimpses of its glory should move us to work diligently toward holiness in the fear of God.
classic_reading:
[Rev.21.1-Rev.21.8]
Chapter 21
Chapter Outline
A new heaven, and new earth: the new Jerusalem where God dwells, and banishes all sorrow from his people. | (1-8) |
Its heavenly origin, glory, and secure defence. | (9-21) |
Its perfect happiness, as enlightened with the presence of God and the Lamb, and in the free access of multitudes, made holy. | (22-27) |
Verses 1-8
The new heaven and the new earth will not be separate from each other; the earth of the saints, their glorified, bodies, will be heavenly. The old world, with all its troubles and tumults, will have passed away. There will be no sea; this aptly represents freedom from conflicting passions, temptations, troubles, changes, and alarms; from whatever can divide or interrupt the communion of saints. This new Jerusalem is the church of God in its new and perfect state, the church triumphant. Its blessedness came wholly from God, and depends on him. The presence of God with his people in heaven, will not be interrupt as it is on earth, he will dwell with them continually. All effects of former trouble shall be done away. They have often been in tears, by reason of sin, of affliction, of the calamities of the church; but no signs, no remembrance of former sorrows shall remain. Christ makes all things new. If we are willing and desirous that the gracious Redeemer should make all things new in order hearts and nature, he will make all things new in respect of our situation, till he has brought us to enjoy complete happiness. See the certainty of the promise. God gives his titles, Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the End, as a pledge for the full performance. Sensual and sinful pleasures are muddy and poisoned waters; and the best earthly comforts are like the scanty supplies of a cistern; when idolized, they become broken cisterns, and yield only vexation. But the joys which Christ imparts are like waters springing from a fountain, pure, refreshing, abundant, and eternal. The sanctifying consolations of the Holy Spirit prepare for heavenly happiness; they are streams which flow for us in the wilderness. The fearful durst not meet the difficulties of religion, their slavish fear came from their unbelief; but those who were so dastardly as not to dare to take up the cross of Christ, were yet so desperate as to run into abominable wickedness. The agonies and terrors of the first death will lead to the far greater terrors and agonies of eternal death.
[Rev.21.9-Rev.21.21]
Verses 9-21
God has various employments for his holy angels. Sometimes they sound the trumpet of Divine Providence, and warn a careless world; sometimes they discover things of a heavenly nature of the heirs of salvation. Those who would have clear views of heaven, must get as near to heaven as they can, on the mount of meditation and faith. The subject of the vision is the church of God in a perfect, triumphant state, shining in its lustre; glorious in relation to Christ; which shows that the happiness of heaven consists in intercourse with God, and in conformity to him. The change of emblems from a bride to a city, shows that we are only to take general ideas from this description. The wall is for security. Heaven is a safe state; those who are there, are separated and secured from all evils and enemies. This city is vast; here is room for all the people of God. The foundation of the wall; the promise and power of God, and the purchase of Christ, are the strong foundations of the safety and happiness of the church. These foundations are set forth by twelve sorts of precious stones, denoting the variety and excellence of the doctrines of the gospel, or of the graces of the Holy Spirit, or the personal excellences of the Lord Jesus Christ. Heaven has gates; there is a free admission to all that are sanctified; they shall not find themselves shut out. These gates were all of pearls. Christ is the Pearl of great price, and he is our Way to God. The street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass. The saints in heaven tread gold under foot. The saints are there at rest, yet it is not a state of sleep and idleness; they have communion, not only with God, but with one another. All these glories but faintly represent heaven.
[Rev.21.22-Rev.21.27]
Verses 22-27
Perfect and direct communion with God, will more than supply the place of gospel institutions. And what words can more full express the union and co-equality of the Son with the Father, in the Godhead? What a dismal world would this be, if it were not for the light of the sun! What is there in heaven that supplies its place? The glory of God lightens that city, and the Lamb is the Light thereof. God in Christ will be an everlasting Fountain of knowledge and joy to the saints in heaven. There is no night, therefore no need of shutting the gates; all is at peace and secure. The whole shows us that we should be more and more led to think of heaven as filled with the glory of God, and enlightened by the presence of the Lord Jesus. Nothing sinful or unclean, idolatrous, or false and deceitful, can enter. All the inhabitants are made perfect in holiness. Now the saints feel a sad mixture of corruption, which hinders them in the service of God, and interrupts their communion with him; but, at their entrance into the holy of holies, they are washed in the laver of Christ's blood, and presented to the Father without spot. None are admitted into heaven who work abominations. It is free from hypocrites, such as make lies. As nothing unclean can enter heaven, let us be stirred up by these glimpses of heavenly things, to use all diligence, and to perfect holiness in the fear of God.

The water and tree of life (verses 1–5)

The streams of comfort we find on earth are often muddy and mixed with trouble.

But the water in this vision is clear and refreshing.

It gives life and preserves the lives of all who drink, flowing forever.

The river pictures the life-giving and sanctifying work of the Holy Spirit, given to sinners through Jesus Christ.

The Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, applying salvation to our souls through his renewing love and power.

The trees of life draw nourishment from the pure river flowing from the throne of God.

God's presence is the health and happiness of the saints in heaven.

The tree represents Christ and all the blessings of his salvation.

The leaves that heal the nations show that God's favor and presence supply every good thing needed in that blessed world.

The devil has no power there.

He cannot draw the saints away from serving God, nor disturb them while they worship.

God and the Lamb are spoken of as one.

Service in heaven brings not only freedom but honor and a share in the kingdom.

There is no night, pain or discouragement.

Worship and enjoyment of God will never be interrupted.

No humanly invented distractions, amusements or pleasures will be needed.

How different this is from merely earthly ideas of heaven—even those that imagine only refined intellectual pleasures!

The sure prophecy and the invitation to come (verses 6–19)

Jesus Christ, speaking through his angel, solemnly confirms the truth of the book and especially the final vision.

He is the faithful and true Lord God.

Holy angels delivered God's message to his holy servants.

The visions concern things that must come to pass, and Christ will come quickly and make their truth evident.

John also received a confirmation from the integrity of the angel who had explained the vision.

When John offered him religious worship, the angel refused and reproved him.

Henry takes this as another testimony against worship directed toward saints and angels, which belongs to God alone.

The Lord calls all people to heed these declarations.

The book is left open, and its words will have an effect.

People devoted to wickedness may grow more hardened, while sincere believers will be strengthened and further sanctified.

Never suppose that lifeless or disobedient faith will save.

The First and the Last pronounces blessing on people who keep his commandments.

The book excludes from heaven the wicked, unjust and especially those who love and practice falsehood.

It cannot itself be dismissed as false without contradicting the solemn testimony it gives.

There is no secure middle state between fidelity to Christ and continuing rebellion against him.

Jesus, the One who gives prophecy, has provided the churches with this light before dawn, assuring them that the brightness of the full day is coming.

The prophecy closes with an open invitation to all humanity to receive freely the gospel's promises and blessings.

The Holy Spirit, speaking through Scripture and working within the conscience of sinners, says, “Come to Christ for salvation.”

The bride, the whole church on earth and in heaven, likewise says, “Come and share our joy.”

No one should hesitate.

Whoever is willing may come and receive the water of life without payment.

May everyone hearing or reading this invitation receive it at once.

The solemn warning at the end condemns anyone who would corrupt God's word by adding to it or taking anything away.

The final promise and blessing (verses 20 and 21)

After making these things known to his people on earth, Christ seems, in Henry's description, to take his leave and return to heaven.

But he assures them that his return is near.

While we carry out our different duties, regardless of the labor, difficulties or grief we face, we can hear our Lord's promise with joy:

“I am coming quickly.”

He will bring an end to the toil and suffering of his faithful servants.

He comes with a reward of grace, generously recompensing every work of faith and every labor of love.

He comes to receive his persevering people into his presence, where they will live with him forever.

Amen. Come, Lord Jesus.

The book ends with a blessing.

Only by Christ's grace can we continue expecting his glory with joy, be prepared for it and be preserved until we receive it.

His appearing will bring joy to those who already share his grace and favor.

May everyone add a sincere Amen.

Let us thirst more earnestly for Jesus' gracious influence in our souls and his presence with us until his grace reaches perfection in glory.

Glory to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, as in the beginning, now and forever.

Amen.
classic_reading:
[Rev.22.1-Rev.22.5]
Chapter 22
Chapter Outline
A description of the heavenly state, under the figures of the water and the tree of life, and of the throne of God and the Lamb.
(1-5)
The truth and certain fulfilling of all the prophetic visions, The Holy Spirit, and the bride, the church, invite, and say, Come.
(6-19)
The closing blessing.
(20-21)
Verses 1-5
All streams of earthly comfort are muddy; but these are clear, and refreshing. They give life, and preserve life, to those who drink of them, and thus they will flow for evermore. These point to the quickening and sanctifying influences of the Holy Spirit, as given to sinners through Christ. The Holy Spirit, proceeding from the Father and the Son, applies this salvation to our souls by his new-creating love and power. The trees of life are fed by the pure waters of the river that comes from the throne of God. The presence of God in heaven, is the health and happiness of the saints. This tree was an emblem of Christ, and of all the blessings of his salvation; and the leaves for the healing of the nations, mean that his favour and presence supply all good to the inhabitants of that blessed world. The devil has no power there; he cannot draw the saints from serving God, nor can he disturb them in the service of God. God and the Lamb are here spoken of as one. Service there shall be not only freedom, but honour and dominion. There will be no night; no affliction or dejection, no pause in service or enjoyment: no diversions or pleasures or man's inventing will there be wanted. How different all this from gross and merely human views of heavenly happiness, even those which refer to pleasures of the mind!
[Rev.22.6-Rev.22.19]
Verses 6-19
The Lord Jesus spake by the angel, solemnly confirming the contents of this book, particularly of this last vision. He is the Lord God faithful and true. Also by his messengers; the holy angels showed them to holy men of God. They are things that must shortly be done; Christ will come quickly, and put all things out of doubt. And by the integrity of that angel who had been the apostle's interpreter. He refused to accept religious worship from John, and reproved him for offering it. This presents another testimony against idolatrous worship of saints and angels. God calls every one to witness to the declarations here made. This book, thus kept open, will have effect upon men; the filthy and unjust will be more so, but it will confirm, strengthen, and further sanctify those who are upright with God. Never let us think that a dead or disobedient faith will save us, for the First and the Last has declared that those alone are blessed who do his commandments. It is a book that shuts out form heaven all wicked and unrighteous persons, particularly those who love and make lies, therefore cannot itself be a lie. There is no middle place or condition. Jesus, who is the Spirit of prophecy, has given his churches this morning-light of prophecy, to assure them of the light of the perfect day approaching. All is confirmed by an open and general invitation to mankind, to come and partake freely of the promises and of the privileges of the gospel. The Spirit, by the sacred word, and by convictions and influence in the sinner's conscience, says, Come to Christ for salvation; and the bride, or the whole church, on earth and in heaven, says, Come and share our happiness. Lest any should hesitate, it is added, Let whosoever will, or, is willing, come and take of the water of life freely. May every one who hears or reads these words, desire at once to accept the gracious invitation. All are condemned who should dare to corrupt or change the word of God, either by adding to it, or taking from it.
[Rev.22.20-Rev.22.21]
Verses 20-21
After discovering these things to his people on earth, Christ seems to take leave of them, and return to heaven; but he assures them it shall not be long before he comes again. And while we are busy in the duties of our different stations of life; whatever labours may try us, whatever difficulties may surround us, whatever sorrows may press us down, let us with pleasure hear our Lord proclaiming, Behold, I come quickly; I come to put an end to the labour and suffering of my servants. I come, and my reward of grace is with me, to recompense, with royal bounty, every work of faith and labour of love. I come to receive my faithful, persevering people to myself, to dwell for ever in that blissful world. Amen, even so, come, Lord Jesus. A blessing closes the whole. By the grace of Christ we must be kept in joyful expectation of his glory, fitted for it, and preserved to it; and his glorious appearance will be joyful to those who partake of his grace and favour here. Let all add, Amen. Let us earnestly thirst after greater measures of the gracious influences of the blessed Jesus in our souls, and his gracious presence with us, till glory has made perfect his grace toward us. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost; as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
